plans.note: Look for a limitation/exclusion of consequential damages and any aggregate cap, typically at the tail of the indemnification article (Art. XVI) or in general provisions (Art. XVIII); confirm mutuality and carve-outs for indemnity, confidentiality and IP infringement.

Art. XVI defines Array Indemnitees and Ono Indemnitees; check that Array (licensor) indemnifies us for third-party IP claims arising from the licensed compounds and for its own negligence/breach, and that our reciprocal indemnity stays narrow (our Territory commercialization acts only). Recall allocation in 16.6 is related but distinct.

Art. VIII 'Certain Covenants' is the likely home of any competing-product or field restriction binding us; also check the grant article and commercialization diligence for implicit non-compete language.

Exclusive licence in our favour is a benefit and should not be flagged; focus on exclusive-sourcing obligations in Art. IX (Product Manufacturing and Supply) requiring us to buy solely from Array, and any covenant in Art. VIII limiting our alternative sourcing.

No MFN language is signalled in the payments, books-and-records or covenants articles; scan Art. VI/VII for any 'most favourable terms' or best-price undertaking running from us to Array before concluding absent.

Collaboration agreements of this type often omit employee non-solicits; check Art. VIII covenants and the general provisions block for a hiring restriction and, if present, confirm term limit and general-advertising carve-out.

Term and Termination (Art. XIII) should contain any at-will termination right; verify we hold a notice-only exit and that Array cannot terminate for convenience mid-term, and cross-check consequences in Art. XIV.

Term likely runs by Initial/Secondary Royalty Term rather than auto-renewal; check Art. XIII for evergreen extension and the Royalty Term definitions in Art. I, and note in the rationale if the structure is expiry-based rather than renewal-based.

Art. XVII Dispute Resolution (referenced as 17.3 and the defined 'Rules') plus the governing law clause in general provisions; assess whether arbitration under foreign rules displaces court venue and whether the chosen law is on the accepted list.

Assignment clause sits in general provisions (Art. XVIII); confirm we may assign to Affiliates and successors without consent and that Array has no termination or renegotiation right on our Change in Control (term defined in Art. I).

Check ownership of Joint Inventions/Joint Know-How and Improvements (Art. XI), Product Trademarks and domain names (Art. XII and Exhibit 12.6), our Data and Ono Know-How treatment (Art. X), and the scope of any Grant-Back License requiring us to assign or exclusively license our results to Array.

Art. II Grant of License: confirm the grant extends to our Affiliates, Sublicensees and Subcontractors in the Ono Territory and is not revocable at Array's discretion; check the Grant-Back License direction and any sublicensing consent gate.

Art. VII (Payments; Books and Records) with the defined 'Auditor' governs Array's audit of our royalty records; test frequency, notice, independent-auditor confidentiality and who bears cost absent a material underpayment threshold.

Look for interest on late payments, milestone forfeiture or penalty payments triggered by our diligence failures in Arts. V–VII and termination consequences; flag only genuine penalties payable by us, not ordinary royalties or late interest.

Art. XV Representations, Warranties and Covenants: check Array's IP title/non-infringement and no-debarment warranties, any product conformance/GMP warranty in Art. IX supply, and whether a broad disclaimer strips the remedy.

Insurance undertakings usually sit at the end of the indemnification article; verify Array carries product liability/clinical trial coverage at commercially reasonable limits, otherwise treat as missing.

Art. IX supply may impose forecast/binding-order or minimum purchase obligations on us, and Art. V may impose Diligent Efforts sales commitments; check for take-or-pay without an exit and any failure-to-meet-minimums consequence.

Art. XIV Effect of Termination with the defined 'Wind-down Period' should cover sell-off rights, transfer of Regulatory Filings and Data, and continued supply during transition; confirm return of our materials and data and that assistance is not conditioned on extra fees.
